title: Past Glory
subtitle: What has been engraved in your mind, seared into your sight, and etched onto your very being.

trails.title: Guide on Emergencies
trails.description: Everyone is curious about the Witch's Garden, and everyone fears it—except for one small bird. To her, it isn't so dangerous.

content.text:
- "Do not touch any plants with barbs."

- Barbs?

- The thing I had to pull off of your leg yesterday.

- "If a plant cuts you and the wound turns purple, or the blood isn't bright red, knock on my window."

- At any time? Even if you're dancing?

- At any time.

- "In the evening, the Critters will lower their top buds to the ground. Try not to step on them."

- Got it! So, can I touch the top buds?

- Do whatever you want. Just don't come crying to me when they bite you.

- "Stop squeezing in through the damaged parts of the fence. Just use the front gate."

- Righto! Didn't know I weren't supposed to ...

- I'm teaching you Arcane Skills so you can fly, not crawl.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text:
Through misty woods, on paths concealed by haze.

He thrice died and thrice was born, in ancient days.

Guide me rightly, that I may not stray.
By the willow fire, a witch is dancing in the ritual ground.
She performs her dance alone. Only the shadows cast by the flames accompany her.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Flowers bear fruit, and beasts give offspring's way.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: With eyes of fire, pierce through the cloudy maze!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Ugh! Failed again. Damn it!
She clenches her right leg, her fingers turning white at the tips.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I won't get anywhere so long as I can't move right.

items.speaker: Vines Carbuncle
items.text: Squeak! Squeak!!
The typically docile Carbuncles are now locked in a frenzied shrieking match. What should have been a calming ritual has quickly turned into a bloodied war drum, and all because of a single misstep.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Enough! The last thing this haunted old place needs is another crazy creature!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow—

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I swear to God—
She collapses by the willow fire, causing the intense flames to suddenly die down. She swiftly grabs a blanket from the pile to cover her legs.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Whatever thing you are, don't think I won't strangle you to death with my bare hands!
She struggles to her feet, but just as she's about to stand, one leg gives way.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Ugh!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ah!
The little girl tumbles through the window and into the room.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Bloody!
She tries to lift herself up for the second time but can only support half of her body. She looks up to find a little face among a pile of stitched and re-stitched clothes.
There could be no more embarrassing or infuriating way for another to behold her.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You! What are you doing here?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I only wanted to show you the arcane skill you taught me.
Flutterpage nimbly gets back on her feet, bouncing around as she shakes off the dust.
Seeing that the girl is unharmed, the witch turns her face, hiding her fleeting look of concern.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But you are in a bad mood, aren't you? What happened? I promise I didn't call you Ms. Willow in front of others!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You said I can call you Ms. Willow when there's just you and me, right?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: And you actually listened? First time for everything, ay? But it's not about what you call me.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Then what is it?
She stares at Willow in confusion. Suddenly, she realizes why she's lying on the ground.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Let me help you up.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I don't need it.
With a flick of her wrist, Willow's coat and hat leap onto her like loyal dogs.
She tries to stand up for a third time, using the rough stone pillar beside her for support, and finally manages to straighten herself out.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So then, if you value my words so highly, what about the time I told you I don't need a knocker-upper?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I remember! You told me, "There's no sense waking me up for anythin'. I don't have any work to go to."

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But I'm not here to wake you up, am I? I already did that for the whole street hours ago!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, have you now? Then maybe you can buzz off and bother someone else. I didn't give my permission to let annoying little flies in my house.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I'm in the middle of something important. So leave me be.
Willow grabs a broom handle and points it toward the window Flutterpage opened.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Just one more question, Miss! I'll be quick.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy and Mr. Fog say you made people sick with the black fog, but I know you didn't do it, did you?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You never told me you can summon black fog.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Done with all that nonsense, are you? If that's all you knocked on my window for—

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But if you didn't, I can tell them the truth.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Or you could even help them find the black fog! You're the best witch I know.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Their problem is no concern of mine.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Em, oh, but I did hear somethin'. I was thinkin' maybe you'd like to hear it, too.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Letter from St. Pavlov Foundation:

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Um, due to ... what? De-teary-on air quality? And arcane tube-or-key-old-kiss ...?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Um. They said the Uluru Qualifiers are canceled.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Stop.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Do you understand at all what you're saying?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: No, but—

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Go away.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Aww ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I said get out!
She seizes Flutterpage with both hands, half dragging, half pulling her toward the open window.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ahhh!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You know what I don't want to hear, eh lass? Your voice!
Flutterpage is flung out the window and carried away like a kite with a broken string on the breeze.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: And your infernal knocking!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Whoaa!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Don't you never take another step into my house, never!
*crash*
The room reverts to its familiar silence, no life save for its solitary resident, just as it has been for the past decade.
Her hastily thrown-on coat and hat slide to the floor as Willow leans on her right leg and limps over to the storage table filled with bottles and jars.
There's still enough mucus left over from yesterday's snails for her to use. She pours the liquid from the jar into the cauldron.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Just a wee bit left.
She sets the fire alight, and the lubricant starts to bubble in the cauldron.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Heh! Eat snails? Hmph!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Let them think what they will. I don't care.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The Fog Hag, a toad monster, the failed work of an ancient alchemist ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Yes, yes, of course. Charlotte O'Hagan, you're nothing but an ugly, evil, terrifying Fog Hag living in a haunted house. You deserve every bit of it.

She lifts her eyes and gazes out the window. To her surprise, she can see the moon, a flurry of small clouds slowly making their way across it, and a flock of silhouetted birds swooping and swerving in tacit harmony.
Like the white sheep that roamed those vast rocky hills. Like the witches in black robes who danced together in perfect unison.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What an age—At last witches no longer need worry about being captured in their sleep, pierced on a stake, or burnt alive.

items.speaker: Announcer
items.text: Our next competitor is our witch from Ireland, a once-in-a-generation talent!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The ancient rituals are different now. We dance, communicating with spirits, like a joyful game.

items.speaker: Announcer
items.text: The Uluru Games—

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Or a graceful competition ...

items.speaker: Announcer
items.text: And the winner for the Floor Ritual is—

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: A desirable ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I left the pot on!
The smell signals a point of no return for the lubricant, and its appearance confirms it as she sees a small blackened mass stuck to the bottom of the cauldron.
Willow's prosthetic leg grinds and creaks as the joints rub up against each other, causing her hip to itch.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Feck! Fecking! Feck!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Fit for the rubbish now!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Rubbish!
